signature: Trying to make an interaction-net runtime (dnx/HVM-style) beat a native strict/lazy evaluator (nix) by reducing monadic plumbing (Freer/IO bind chains) away IN THE NET
resolution: DEAD END (deepwiki-verified twice vs HigherOrderCO/HVM source cmp.rs): interaction nets do NOT eliminate monadic plumbing — HVM has no supercompiler/partial-eval/cross-REF-inlining; every IO/bind survives to runtime as a CALL interaction. Nets RELOCATE the monad into the net, re-pricing it UP (~5x a native op, up to 100x on alloc-free loops; nets only win on massive parallelism / optimal-sharing / heavy short-lived alloc — NOT small strict programs, which is the evaluator's home turf). The correct lever for a statically-closed bind chain is COMPILE-TIME SPECIALIZATION in the lowering (partial-eval / monomorphize the kleisli dict / inline bind+return / beta-reduce the closed spine once) — compiler work, NOT engine work. Also: nix-unit is single-threaded (nrWorkers=1 dead field, nix-unit.cc:95) + cache-less + pays ~25-30ms createBaseEnv startup per spawn; the winning move vs it is STRUCTURAL wall-clock asymmetry (content-addressed result cache for re-runs + daemon to amortize startup), NOT out-reducing its evaluator.

signature: jj multi-workspace land → empty commits (agent edits never snapshotted)
resolution: jj snapshots ONLY the workspace whose dir you run a command in. Agents (correctly) never run jj, so their working-copy edits in an isolated `jj workspace add` dir are NOT in that workspace's @ commit until a jj command runs IN that dir. Landing (rebase/squash) those @ commits from the MAIN workspace lands EMPTY commits (describe message only, zero content); `jj workspace forget` then orphans the on-disk files. SYMPTOM: landed commit message claims a crate/file but it's absent from main; `jj diff -r <rev> --stat` shows 0 files. FIX (mandatory land protocol): BEFORE landing any agent's workspace, run a jj command IN that workspace dir (`cd <ws>; jj status`) to snapshot, then verify `jj diff -r @ --stat` is NON-EMPTY. RECOVERY if already landed empty: files persist on disk in the (even forgotten) workspace dir → `jj op restore <pre-land-op>`, `jj new main`, cp the real files into main tree, `jj describe`, verify `jj diff -r @ --stat` has them, advance main. ALWAYS verify landed tree contains the claimed code (verify-don't-trust caught this).

APPLY cannot parallelize on CPU: Arena is a single shared allocator (slots/live/next/eraser_count) — footprint-disjointness is over NodeIndex SETS not allocator state, so disjoint pairs still both mutate live-list/next. main.md:[L337-339] (perfect confluence) licenses REORDERING the rewrite relation + same interaction count, NOT concurrent mutation of one allocator. Only the PLAN phase parallelizes — all 6 planners (annihilate_fans/reps_into, erase_into, commute_rep_fan/rep_rep_into, aux_fan_replication_into) are pure &Arena, no scratch write. GPU+pod-mirror is the ONLY way to parallelize apply (disjoint slot scatter, no allocator). Do NOT attempt rayon par_iter over &mut Arena apply.
